thread:
amy: Heads up — planning Korea pilot capacity + reserve/burst policy. Need quick alignment: who can weigh in on reserve sizing vs burst credits, enterprise carveouts, and cache warm strategy? Target: pilot in ~6 weeks.
jasper: Can do. Quick q: do we expect steady-state QPS for pilot ~200 r/s or more spiky? We have EU pilot telemetry but different footprint.
liam: Sales estimate -> initial customers ~3 enterprise pilots + a few mid-market apps. Typical spiky peaks ~300 r/s per tenant. I’d plan for 600r/s baseline if we want headroom.
priya: 600 reserve sounds pricey for a pilot. Alternative: smaller reserve + larger burst credit bucket and strict routing policies to protect enterprise.
devops-bot: vendor capacity snapshot: korea-zone-1 spot availability ~85%, eviction risk ~15% during APAC business hours.
sarah-mgr: @amy what latency SLOs are we promising for the pilot? that will drive local reserve needs.
amy: SLA targets: p50 < 90ms, p95 < 350ms. Enterprise pilot gets 99.9% uptime on a dedicated local pool. Public pilot allowed fallback to EU for best-effort.
jasper: With those SLOs, local reserve for enterprise is non-negotiable. Public traffic can use burst and fallback routing. Need clear fallback policy to avoid cascading latencies.
liam: Also: KV cache cold starts matter. If we pre-warm top prefixes per tenant (top-5), we can shave ~40ms p50 and reduce token compute spikes.
priya: Pre-warm job is cheap — schedule synthetic requests against model endpoints during off-peak. Ops runway minimal. We should codify prompts per tenant.
amy: Operational asks (deliverables by EOD Fri): 1) reserve vs burst policy draft, 2) routing/fallback config proposal, 3) cache-warm runbook, 4) cost estimate for 6-week pilot. Can team take these?
jasper: I'll draft the reserve/burst policy. Quick sketch below, will refine:
```
reserve: 50% baseline (600 r/s)
burst_pool: credit bucket 400 r/s
enterprise_isolation: dedicated pool 200 r/s
fallback: route->eu with latency guard (p95 threshold)
```
I'll turn this into a config PR.
liam: I'll own cache-warm runbook + autoscaler guardrails. Question: grace period on eviction drain? proposing 30s to flush KV and migrate in-flight requests.
priya: I'll produce the cost estimate. If we keep reserve at 50% baseline, monthly pilot delta ~ $XXk — will replace XX with vendor numbers. Also will model a 30% burst usage scenario.
amy: Procurement ask: can we secure any committed h100-equivalent capacity in Korea with vendor A for the pilot? If lead time >6 weeks we need Plan B. @jasper follow up with procurement.
jasper: pinged procurement and vendor-A. Will share ETA.
devops-bot: vendor-A portal: estimated lead time 9 weeks for requested SKU.
sarah-mgr: :thinking_face: 9 weeks > pilot window. Plan B: ephemeral burst through cloud partner + traffic shaping + stronger fallbacks. Also consider temporary dedicated in eu with cross-region routing for enterprise credits.
amy: Scope negotiation summary: enterprise pilot -> small local dedicated commit for strict SLOs; public pilot -> burst + eu fallback; cache-warm mandatory; procurement follow-up to confirm local capacity. Reconvene Fri 10:00 to review drafts.
jasper: ack, will have policy draft and procurement notes.
liam: ack, runbook + autoscaler config in draft.
priya: ack, cost sheet incoming.
sarah-mgr: i'll join Fri review and coordinate sales/customer comms for carveouts.
amy: thanks everyone. If procurement changes, update thread so we can re-run cost calc. :thumbsup:
